title: A blue wave is building as the G.O.P.’s numbers sink
gist: A short paywalled teaser argues a Democratic blue wave is building ahead of the 2026 midterms as the war in Iran proves unpopular and prices rise. Every Republican Senate candidate in New York Times polling is underwater, so a Democratic Senate majority is within reach but not secure.

insights.claim: Every Republican Senate candidate polled by the New York Times ahead of the 2026 midterms has net-negative favorability.
insights.speaker: Halina Bennet
insights.so_what: Raises the odds of a Democratic Senate, and with it gridlock or a policy shift in 2027.
insights.quote: every Republican Senate candidate the Times polled is underwater

insights.claim: The unpopular war in Iran and rising prices are driving the Republican polling slump heading into the 2026 midterms.
insights.speaker: Halina Bennet
insights.so_what: Ties geopolitical conflict and inflation directly to election risk for the governing party.
insights.quote: With the war in Iran unpopular and prices rising

insights.claim: Democrats' chances of winning a Senate majority in 2026 have never looked better, though the path remains narrow and the outcome far from secure.
insights.speaker: Halina Bennet
insights.so_what: Investors should price in more chance of a split Congress, but not treat it as the base case.
insights.quote: Democrats’ odds of walking the narrow path to a Senate majority have never looked better.

insights.claim: Sherrod Brown is the Democratic Senate candidate in Ohio in 2026, one of the races on Democrats' narrow path to a Senate majority.
insights.speaker: Halina Bennet
insights.so_what: Ohio is a key race to watch for Senate control.
